subject: BridgePath renewal — SLA top-up and one-time credit request
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Subject: BridgePath renewal — request for SLA top-up + one-time credit

Irene — quick escalation for DP-4821 (BridgePath). Renewal due 8/15. Customer is asking for: a) 10% one-time credit on new annual invoice, b) SLA top-up (99.95% -> 99.99%) for 12 months, and c) reset to 12-month term starting today to align with their procurement cycle.

Context: they saw a spike in inference latency during a region outage in May; CS has been mitigating with model routing and caching recommendations. Usage is up ~85% YoY and they're contemplating moving part of production off Redwood if we can't provide contractual stability. They are a mid-market account (annualized base $420k last year).

Proposed internal ask: authorize 10% credit + SLA top-up (technical acceptance criteria / SLO addendum) and allow a 12-month term reset. If we can get exec sign-off today, I can push a clean PO and avoid them re-evaluating vendors.

Attachments: BridgePath_Renewal_Proposal_v3.pdf, bridgepath_usage_Q2.csv

Ben
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — I have a couple of clarifying questions before I take this to finance/legal: 
1) Can you confirm the requested 10% credit is a one-time invoice-level credit (not on-going discount)?
2) Do we have telemetry showing the May incident impact by customer team (tokens lost, error rates, time windows)? I want concrete impact to justify SLA uplift.
3) What is the requested SLA remedy structure (credit tiers / measurement windows) — legal will need the exact language.

If you can reply with the items above and a short risk/benefit bullet list I’ll prioritize the review.

Irene

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: BridgePath renewal — request for SLA top-up + one-time credit

Answers below and pasted excerpt from BridgePath procurement note (for context):

Q1: One-time invoice-level credit of 10% off the first renewed annual invoice. Not a permanent unit price change.

Q2: Telemetry: attached "bridgepath_usage_Q2.csv" includes a high-level breakdown. Summary: on 2027-05-12 03:22-03:46 UTC we saw a regional backend capacity failover affecting us-west-2; BridgePath had ~22% of their production traffic routed to fallback that increased token latency by ~1.8x for that window. Their SRE measured ~0.6% request error spike for that 24-minute window and logged 12 support tickets internally.

Q3: Requested SLA addendum: 99.99% monthly availability for the routes used in production; remedy = 10% service credit on monthly invoice if availability < 99.99% in a month, escalated credit (25%) if availability < 99.9%. Legal will need precise SLO definition (we can mirror our standard doc with thresholds bumped).

Risk/benefit bullets:
- Upside: avoid churn risk; saves ~$420k ARR; protects east-coast pilot expansion next quarter.
- Downside: SLA bump increases our obligation but limited to 12 months + only on routes they route to Redwood; financial exposure small if measured correctly (we estimate < $35k expected credit risk annually based on their traffic pattern).

BridgePath procurement snippet (copied):
> We need contractual reassurance we can run predictable workloads. If Redwood will provide a one-time concession and the 99.99% SLO for 12 months, we'll sign the PO this week and plan expansion.

Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-11T08:29:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BridgePath renewal — request for SLA top-up + one-time credit

Irene — CS and I recommend approving this under the following guardrails: 
- Credit = one-time, applied to the first invoice only; require signed PO + updated MSA addendum.
- SLA addendum limited to a single region set (us-west-2 + fallback exclusions) and valid for 12 months only.
- Term reset allowed to align billing, but do not change the committed minimum (keep their committed spend floor identical to prior FY).
- Add a launch checklist: routing policy pinned, KV cache enabled for their top-10 routes, and scheduled weekly health sync for first 90 days.

This balances risk and gives them the operational controls they asked for. If legal can draft the addendum with these constraints I support moving forward.

Marissa
Customer Success Director
Redwood Inference
